commits.message:
[task-curation] Grade Snowball panels locally and build EvalLite (#10926)

Add EvalLite, a 1,500-task evaluation set for Snowball RL, and make the
910-task development panel gradable on the training job's machines. RL
runs need a held-out score they can compute without container images or
a judge service, from tasks that tuning never looks at.

- EvalLite. A fixed sample of public benchmarks: MATH500, AIME24,
MMLU-Pro, GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval+, MBPP+, IFEval, IFBench, and 165 NeMo
next-tool-call tasks, plus a 100-task fast subset. It compares
checkpoints of one model; it is not a headline benchmark and does not
cover multi-turn agent work or long context. A next-tool-call task
scores only the exact function name with exact JSON arguments; the
starting model passes 19.2% of those answers, inside the recipe's 5%–95%
rule. `python -m experiments.post_training.task_curation.driver --corpus
CORPUS.json --eval-lite RECIPE.json` builds it, skipping tasks that
match training or development tasks. [The EvalLite
reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/docs/references/task-curation.md#evallite)
lists the parts and how to change them.
- Local graders. EvalLite and development-panel tasks grade in process
or in a Python package environment; the build fails on one that needs a
container image or judge service. A development task written for an
image takes the package environment of a training task from its dataset.
- Training selection. A recipe lists the development panel under
`heldout` and other evaluation files under `exclusions`, and a training
task matching any of them by ID, public semantics, context or
whitespace-normalized final user statement is left out. The checked-in
recipe, version `2026.11.10.1` (not yet built), excludes the development
panel and EvalLite, and gives the 6,653 tasks of the AI-judged glaive
code-assistant source to `eurus2_code` (16,970 tasks), so all 100,000
tasks grade locally.
- Records. EvalLite and the development panel each publish a task
manifest and grader-kind counts.

The benchmark tasks come from the catalog's existing Evalchemy corpora,
and the NeMo source wraps the existing `taskcompendium` importer.

The published
[snowball-100k@2026.11.04.1](s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/task-selection/snowball-100k/2026.11.04.1/summary.json)
([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Frl-data%2Ftask-selection%2Fsnowball-100k%2F2026.11.04.1%2Fsummary.json))
predates EvalLite and holds 100,000 locally graded tasks; EvalLite
excludes it and the development panel, and its [data
audit](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-rlci-e12-final-panel-audit-20261104-235011)
verifies zero overlap. Replaying 867 development rollouts through the
local graders reproduced every stored score
([results](s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/atqamar/experiments/snowball-panel-local-graders/20261026-202022-cd3f43a4a6/results.json),
[Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fatqamar%2Fexperiments%2Fsnowball-panel-local-graders%2F20261026-202022-cd3f43a4a6%2Fresults.json)).
With starting checkpoint
`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21`, a [greedy
evaluation](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-rlci-e12-qualification-tools-20261104-225223%2Fcheckpoints-snowball-rl-e12-qualification-final-2026.11.04.2-eb7b3fac01c4)
scored all 1,500 tasks without grading errors and an [eight-answer
measurement](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-rlci-e12-pass-rates-20261104-230104%2Fcheckpoints-snowball-rl-e12-pass-rates-2026.11.04.2-cd4297a836cd)
scored 11,356 of 12,000 answers; [CPU
regrading](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-rlci-e12-grading-repair-20261104-233326)
scored the 644 whose verifiers timed out (cause not isolated). The
published [EvalLite
`2026.11.11.1`](s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/task-selection/eval-lite/2026.11.11.1/summary.json)
([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Frl-data%2Ftask-selection%2Feval-lite%2F2026.11.11.1%2Fsummary.json))
pins [those
scores](s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/selection-inputs/eval-lite/pass-rates/2026.11.04.2/pass_rates.parquet)
([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Frl-data%2Fselection-inputs%2Feval-lite%2Fpass-rates%2F2026.11.04.2%2Fpass_rates.parquet)).
Both runs used the task files of build `2026.11.04.2`; the [EvalLite
build](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fatqamar%2Fatqamar-rlci-p60-eval-lite-20261111-054715)
verified that `2026.11.11.1` has the same Parquet bytes.

Other curation users: a recipe's `heldout` is a list of files, each with
a `format`; `train_quick_loop.py` keeps its pinned
`snowball-100k@2026.11.04`.

#10957 moves the Evalchemy modules the EvalLite tests import; whichever
merges second uses the resulting paths. Published EvalLite stores each
task with its grader, so grader changes elsewhere reach it only through
a new EvalLite version.

commits.message:
[rl] Run curated closure rows under the assistant-prefix harness (#11062)

Curated closure rows train under Shellbox, while `panel-910` of draft PR
[#10747](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10747) scores
closure tasks under the assistant-prefix harness, so training and
evaluation give the model different prompts. A task whose context ends
in an assistant message now runs under the assistant-prefix harness, the
rule that open PR
[#10622](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10622) uses in
`lower_feed_task`. Such a task needs this harness whatever its dataset
is called, so `harness_by_dataset` is gone.


[`_canonical_task_prompt`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ca7f3f4bdd37a8075aaf16a75908014c9be2798/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/dataset/tasks.py#L189)
picks the harness by `task.source.dataset`, and
[`default.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ca7f3f4bdd37a8075aaf16a75908014c9be2798/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/config/task_session_config/default.yaml#L21-L23)
maps only `structure-closure` to this harness.
[Curation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ca7f3f4bdd37a8075aaf16a75908014c9be2798/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/conversion.py#L28-L34)
sets `source.dataset` to [the source
repository](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ca7f3f4bdd37a8075aaf16a75908014c9be2798/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/structure_closure.py#L17).
So all 11,634 closure rows of
[`snowball-100k`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ca7f3f4bdd37a8075aaf16a75908014c9be2798/experiments/post_training/task_curation/recipes/snowball-100k.json#L39)
load under Shellbox, which ends the assistant turn and adds the user
turn "Give your answer as plain text." The grader still scores `prefix +
reply`.

On #10747's start model, `Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21`, at
temperature 1.0, the 243 `panel-910` closure tasks score 0.222 under the
assistant-prefix harness and 0.069 under Shellbox (difference 0.153, 95%
interval 0.110 to 0.198). On a small proxy model, the prompt also
changes what training teaches. We trained `Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507` with
verl for 300 RLOO steps on 12,000 closure rows of
`Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data`, the release behind
`snowball-100k`'s closure rows, and ran each prompt with two seeds.
Under the assistant-prefix prompt, greedy replies to the 243 closure
tasks scored 0.42 before training, 0.86 and 0.88 after prefix training,
and 0.36 and 0.23 after Shellbox training. Prefix training scored 0.58
higher (95% interval 0.53 to 0.63). The first comment gives the details.

Rows do not change, so no new curation or selection is needed.
`panel-910` keeps its prompts and grades, because [the panel's closure
rows](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1ca7f3f4bdd37a8075aaf16a75908014c9be2798/experiments/post_training/task_curation/inventory.py#L118-L124)
already run under the assistant-prefix harness and end in an assistant
message. Training prompts change on the 11.6% of rows that are closure
rows, so runs on this branch differ from #10747's pinned controls. Draft
PR #11032 already requires new control runs, so those runs could train
closure rows under the assistant-prefix harness. Merge after #11058,
which cuts the stop token that can leave a closing code fence open. We
have not run SkyRL training on this branch.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[shellbox] Add process scopes for delegated local cgroups (#11275)

Add a machine-owned process scope that groups agent commands and the
background descendants they leave running. Termination rejects new
scoped commands and waits until every scoped descendant has exited
before returning. Callers can then collect outputs or run verification.
Setup services and verifier commands remain outside the scope.

Local machines implement scopes in delegated cgroup v2 hierarchies. Each
command has a child cgroup: a command timeout or cancellation kills its
descendants while preserving background work from earlier commands and
allowing new commands in the scope. Docker, gVisor, Iris, Daytona, QEMU,
and ShellSim reject scope creation until they provide confirmed
descendant teardown. Harbor integration remains in #10735.

Part of #9873.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Typed recipes (3/4): Build experiment recipes from typed classes (#9749)

Build each RL experiment's SkyRL recipe with the typed classes from 2/4.
A wrong key, value type, or option value fails when the experiment is
built, before anything is submitted to Iris, with an error that names
the field.

Experiments build their recipes with `SkyRLRecipe` or
`SkyRLRecipe.from_document` and pass the resulting YAML to `SkyRLSpec`.
The async presets and Canary apply command-line settings with
`with_settings`, which parses each value by its field's type. A mapping
value is a JSON object and merges into the existing mapping, and an
empty value is not read as null. This PR does not modify `SkyRLSpec` or
the launch document format. A `--set` key is a schema field path,
written without Hydra's `+` prefix. Marin checks model geometry and role
plans itself; the recipe classes do not. `async_rl` takes a `--seed`
option that sets the launch seed; `trainer.seed` is not a `--set` key.
The library is in Marin's test dependency group, and the published
`marin-core` package does not depend on it.

After the launcher loads them, every launch and task document built by
the experiments is identical to the one built at main `3a3a2e1ab2`.

[marina] Add a model scorecard for policy eval results (#11254)

Add a static Marina app that shows selected models' scores on the 18
eval-policy chat benchmarks from #10197, on a 0–100 scale with two
decimals. Each score links to its EvalDash run page. A result that is
not an eval run, such as a regrade, links to its raw files in Filer
instead. Each model name links to the Hugging Face revision that was
evaluated.

`scorecard.yaml` lists the rows, columns and run behind each cell, and
labels each cell official (run under the eval-policy pin) or unofficial
(run from Marin main outside the pin). `build_data.py` reads each cited
run's record with CoreWeave credentials, applies the published
measurement policy, and checks the run's status, benchmark and model
revision. It writes the checked-in `scorecard.json`. The release build
embeds that JSON in the page, so releasing never reads object storage.
Adding a model or updating a cell is an edit to `scorecard.yaml` plus
regenerated `scorecard.json`.

The first rows are Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B, DeepSeek V4 Flash
and Muse Glimmer 30B, with 33 of 54 cells filled. All are unofficial
runs from main. The remaining cells name why they are empty: runs in
progress, the gated GPQA dataset, or V4 Flash's MRCR, which the harness
cannot score without a Jinja chat template. Glimmer's gsm8k score will
be affected by #11226 once its run finishes.

The app has not been released. After merge, the first release uses
`--base-version 0` for the declared UUID.

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Typed recipes (2/4): Add a typed SkyRL recipe library (#10642)

Add a library of typed classes for SkyRL training recipes. A recipe
built with these classes rejects unknown keys, wrong value types,
out-of-range values such as a negative rollout staleness, values outside
SkyRL's options (for example an advantage estimator other than `grpo`,
`rloo`, and the other registered ones), and keys the launcher sets
itself. The error names the field or the `--set` setting, and when a
document or setting names a launcher-owned key, the owner. Without these
classes, the launcher rejects unknown keys and checks only the context
budget, engine options, entrypoint, and some algorithm settings before
submission; a wrong type or value in most other fields is first seen by
the trainer on the GPU job.

Marin experiments write recipes and the vendored SkyRL launcher reads
them, but Marin cannot import SkyRL, which has its own environment and
GPU dependencies. Both therefore import this library. It lives in
`lib/skyrlrecipe` and depends only on Pydantic. The Marin workspace
installs it as a member, `vendor/skyrl` installs it by path, and it is
not published.

Most classes, in `sections.py` and `sampling.py`, are generated from
SkyRL's YAML defaults and Hydra config groups by
`vendor/skyrl/scripts/generate_recipe_schema.py`, so the schema follows
SkyRL's own config. `vendor/skyrl/scripts/recipe_schema_sidecar.py`
supplies types the YAML cannot express. A test regenerates the file and
fails if the committed copy differs, so a SkyRL config change must
update the schema in the same PR. The hand-written code covers typed
classes for teachers, callbacks, and off-policy correction rules, which
the YAML does not declare, the context-length budget, parsing
command-line settings by field type, the table of launcher-owned keys,
and messages that name the replacement for retired keys.
`docs/dev-guide/skyrl.md` describes how to regenerate.

Experiments use the library in 3/4 and the launcher in 4/4.

Part of marin-community/MarinSkyRL#933.

commits.author: HRL9000
commits.message:
[finelog] Forward rows named for the sender's own cluster (#11176)

The Finelog forwarder now also sends rows whose `cluster` is the
sender's own `forwarding.cluster`, not only rows where it is empty or
NULL. Rows naming another cluster are still skipped. This change is a
no-op, based on our deployment configuration today.

Finelog rows written on the marin (GCP) cluster have an empty `cluster`,
while rows from the other clusters carry names such as `cw-rno2a`.
That's because the forwarder sends only rows with an empty `cluster` and
fills in the sender's name as it forwards. Every writer therefore leaves
the column blank so its rows stay eligible. marin is the hub and doesn't
forward, so its own rows are never named. The result is awkward for
readers and writers alike:

- Queries on the hub have to treat empty as marin. 47 Grafana queries do
it with `COALESCE(NULLIF(cluster, ''), 'marin')`, and 13 more label the
same rows `'unknown'` or `'local'`.
- A writer needs to enforce this unintuitive rule of not filling out the
cluster field. because on a forwarding server, logs that have the field
filled in would be silently dropped by the forwarding rule and never
reach the hub.

This PR lets a server's own named rows through the filter. A follow-up
will stamp the cluster name where rows are written instead of in the
forwarder, so marin's own rows carry `marin` instead of an empty value.

Today's servers forward exactly what they forward now: the CoreWeave
senders' rows are all empty, and `marin`, the only server that receives
forwarded rows (a `jwt` auth layer), doesn't forward. Attribution
doesn't change either. The forwarder already rewrites `cluster` to its
own `forwarding.cluster` on every row it ships, and the hub overwrites
it again from the sender's JWT. Rows relayed from another cluster carry
that cluster's name, so the filter still keeps them from being sent on
again, and no startup check is needed against a server that both
receives and forwards rows.

The scan in `forwarding.rs` adds `OR cluster = <forwarding.cluster>`,
quoted with the existing `sql_literal` helper. Tests cover a row named
for the sender's cluster (forwarded under that name), an unnamed row
(stamped), a row naming another cluster (not forwarded), and a cluster
name containing a quote. `OPS.md` and `AGENTS.md` describe the rule.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[inference] Prepare Hugging Face weights for direct marin-serve iris

`marin-serve iris` prepares Hugging Face checkpoints on CPU before submitting a direct server when a target cluster is pinned, or when a TPU serve pins one region. Without those placement constraints it warns and keeps the worker's own download, avoiding a CPU mirror in an unrelated cache. Root GPU submissions without a cluster pin skip preparation because the serving job can auto-federate while the CPU job stays local. In-job GPU children keep preparing without that pin. TPU preparation without a cluster pin requires one explicit region, or an unset region inherited from a parent job; unrestricted regions and unset root placement skip with a warning.

The CLI and `remote_inference` share `prepare_hf_models`. Each model keeps its own pinned commit. A colocated coordinator can reuse a complete snapshot without submitting a CPU job; a CLI launch prepares through its Iris client. The CPU job uses the CLI’s workspace checkout when available; otherwise it installs the CLI’s marin-core version. Preparation failure or cancellation stops the prepare jobs and prevents server submission. Brokered serving continues to prepare inside `remote_inference`.

Direct launches also use an explicit `--secret HF_TOKEN env:MODEL_TOKEN` for revision lookup and CPU preparation. Preparation receives only that explicit secret, through Iris secret files; other explicit secrets go only to serving. The token stays out of the model config and preparation callable arguments.

An explicit CoreWeave `target_cluster` on the serving resources still submits a CPU job when warm: the local controller reports its cluster as `local`, which cannot prove a named match. Eval children leave that field unset, inherit their orchestrator’s cluster, and can reuse a warm cache in-process. A warm `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` probe on cw-rno2a (`/karan/task380-warm-prepare-7777b7b37f`) took 64.7 s client-observed, including a 4.8 s submit RPC. Controller timestamps show 25.0 s from submission to code start (including about 1.7 s setup), 9.7 s for imports and cache checks, and 18.3 s from code completion to terminal status. The warm resolver itself took 0.12 s. This probe included a federation hop from marin; a local CoreWeave orchestrator skips that hop. No serving accelerators were reserved.

`--target-cluster marin` without a region passes the placement guard, but that GCP cluster spans several regions, so preparation and serving can still use different regional caches.

Builds on #10277. See the [evaluation guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20261109-serve-precache/docs/tutorials/run-lm-evals.md) for cache-placement limits and the [pre-caching design](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-rRhP9mB4hpbzXwxUfPUTejwUVk1w68BOIs9TWdsBFk/edit).

The combined preparation/cache regressions pass all 43 cases, including explicit-token success and access failures without ambient HF credentials. The affected run completed all 1,486 selected cases: 1,477 passed, 5 failed, 4 skipped, and 0 unfinished. The five task-driver failures match the independently reproduced main failures because the local Python lacks `os.pidfd_open`. Formatting, lint, type checks, and the strict documentation build pass. The optional Read the Docs build was cancelled externally after 69 seconds and left its GitHub status pending; all 21 completed checks passed. An independent source review found no actionable correctness or security issues; live private-model Iris validation has not been run.

Part of #9233

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[training] Account for supervised tokens in ordered chat mixtures (#10705)

Add `marin.training.chat_token_accounting`, which counts the supervised
(loss-bearing) tokens in rendered chat rows. Each row is rendered with
the dataset component's training preprocessor, and the counts come from
its assistant loss mask. The caller labels each row, with one label for
the final assistant reply and one for earlier assistant turns. For an
explicit order of rows and a batch size, the module reports each label's
pooled share of supervised tokens. It also reports the mean, across
updates, of that label's share of each update's supervised tokens. This
mean is the label's cross-entropy coefficient mass. It does not estimate
gradient share.

The counts must match training. The module checks the dataset
component's effective packing the same way training does, and it rejects
packed components. It also rejects rows longer than the context, a chat
template that differs from the pinned hash, and rows whose token IDs or
masks differ from the training preprocessor's output. It does not change
the input rows.

The Snowball identity SFT runs mix identity answers with preservation
and replay rows. Before the first run we froze the training stream and
recorded the share of each update's supervised tokens that came from
identity answers. Raw token counts do not give this share, because the
loss mask decides which tokens count. For example, the first 128 rows
held 3,383 identity tokens out of 87,905 supervised tokens ([training
worker](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-sft-m16-reading-chukar-md)).

commits.message:
[levanter] Add an FP32-activations flag to Snowball (#10687)

Add `SnowballConfig.fp32_activations`. When it is set, Snowball computes
each SiLU and sigmoid in float32 and casts the result to the input dtype
once. This covers the embed, final and per-block GatedNorms, the
attention head gate, the shared MLP and the routed experts. The flag
defaults to False, which keeps the current activations in the compute
dtype.

In a bfloat16 forward, XLA rounds inside these activations. The torch
reference for the Snowball identity experiments computes them in
float32. At layer 0, rounding inside the activation changed 29-36% of
elements at each SiLU and sigmoid site. With float32 activations and one
cast, the count fell to 0 at each site
([diagnostic](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-l0-levanter-r2-reading-chukar-md)).
On the full model, Levanter's expert-set agreement with vLLM rose from
0.898 to 0.912, level with torch against vLLM (0.912).

The flag raises an error with `moe_implementation="sonic_cute"`, because
that kernel fuses a bfloat16 SiLU. Like `router_dot_fp32`, the flag is
not written to HF metadata, and `preserve_hf_runtime_settings` keeps it
when the config reloads from HF.

Part of #10695

commits.author: mminutoli
commits.message:
[grug] Leave the MoE ring padding rows outside every ragged_dot group (#11125)

Leave unused ring and ring_filtered dispatch capacity outside every
expert group. The old group sizes assigned those padding rows to the
final expert, making it roughly four times the average group in June 67B
MI355X runs and computing matmul rows that no caller reads.

`ragged_dot` is unchanged: rows after `sum(group_sizes)` stay
unspecified, and no implementation masks or zeroes them, so standalone
`ragged_dot` (Megablox on TPU included) costs what it did before. The
ring paths read only valid rows: `ring`'s scatter-add combine now drops
the padding rows, and `ring_gather_combine` and `ring_filtered` already
gather valid rows only. A test fills the rows past the groups, and their
lhs gradient, with NaN and checks every ring path against a zero fill.

At June shapes, with the earlier version of this PR (which also zeroed
those rows inside `ragged_dot`), ring and ring_filtered
forward-plus-backward time fell 4.3–11.5% on H100, GB200, and TPU v4-8.
[Benchmark](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11125#issuecomment-6779373873).

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[levanter, marin] Add a rocm extra that installs JAX 0.12 on AMD (#11052)

Add a `rocm` extra to marin-levanter and marin-core, so AMD nodes
install from the lockfile with `uv sync --all-packages --extra rocm
--no-dev`. It replaces the AMD README's hand-run `uv pip install` steps.
The extra pins JAX 0.12.0 with the ROCm 10 plugin from PyPI, jax-triton
0.3.1, Triton 3.6.0, and the ROCm 10.1.0 runtime with gfx942 and gfx950
device libraries from AMD's TheRock index.

AMD needs JAX 0.12 for jax_triton kernels on multi-GPU nodes. Before
0.12, the ROCm plugin deletes each compiled jax_triton kernel file on
its first launch without holding a lock. A process that launches a new
kernel on several GPUs at once then fails on the missing file or hangs
at the next collective (#9853).

The other install targets keep their JAX. `rocm` is declared as
conflicting with the `cpu`, `gpu`, `tpu` and `pipeline` extras and with
the iris and fray test groups that pin JAX 0.11.1, so uv resolves it
separately; `--no-dev` is required for that reason. Exported package
lists for the existing targets are unchanged apart from one Windows-only
marker on `pywinpty`:

| Install target | JAX |
|---|---|
| default, `cpu`, `tpu`, `gpu` | 0.11.1 |
| `pipeline` | 0.11.0 |
| `rocm` | 0.12.0 |

marin-core's JAX cap rises to `<0.13` to match Levanter. The extra lists
the four `rocm-sdk-*` packages directly because uv applies index sources
only to direct dependencies. Most of the `uv.lock` diff is rewritten
resolution markers for the new extra.

On one Vultr node with 8x MI355X, a fresh `uv sync --extra rocm` from
this branch took 13 minutes; JAX then reported 8 MI355X devices and ran
a bf16 matmul and a jax_triton kernel on all 8 GPUs on first launch. The
kernel runs below used the same versions installed by the earlier `uv
pip install` recipe. Each ran from a cold start (fresh process, empty
Triton cache) and compared outputs and gradients against a JAX
reference; the repro row is the standalone script from #9853.

| Kernel, 8 GPUs, cold start | jax 0.11.1 | jax 0.12.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Standalone race repro | hangs | 3/3 pass |
| QBRoutedMoE top-k | 1/3 runs fail on the deleted file | 3/3 pass |
| Sonic gather/combine, forward and backward | 3/3 pass | 3/3 pass |
| Ragged all-to-all MoE, forward and backward | 3/3 fail on the deleted
file | 3/3 pass |
| Pooled all-to-all MoE, forward and backward | 3/3 hang at a collective
| 3/3 pass |
| `gpu_triton_flash` (#11053), forward and backward | 1/3 runs fail on
the deleted file | 3/3 pass |

We have not tested the extra on the HPC Fund MI350X or MI325X nodes.
Stacked on #11046; merge it first.

---------

Co-authored-by: Amy Sartran <users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[ci] Run the Snowball parity H100 leg on cw-rno2a as github-iris (#11220)

Every scheduled run of the Snowball vLLM parity nightly has failed on
its H100 leg since the workflow landed, from 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-11
([latest](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/43088352309)).
The leg logs in with the `iris-ci-smoke` key and federates its root to
`cw-us-east-02a`. That cluster doesn't admit that account:

```
Error: Peer cw-us-east-02a rejected the handoff: Submitter 'iris-ci-smoke@***.iam.gserviceaccount.com' is not admitted for federation to this cluster
```

The CoreWeave nightlies do this differently. SkyRL/CatCount on
`cw-rno2a` and Hero GB200 on `cw-us-east-08a` log in through Workload
Identity as `github-iris`, which those clusters admit. This PR does the
same for the GPU leg and moves it to `cw-rno2a`. No allowlist change,
and no controller rollout. The TPU leg keeps its key.

The failure-diagnostics step also exited early (`GCP diagnostics require
--project and --controller-label`). It now passes `--controller-label
iris-marin-controller`, as the other canaries do.

Open check: the Snowball export lives in `s3://marin-us-east-02a`, so
the H100 leg now reads its weights from another CoreWeave region. A
`workflow_dispatch` run on this branch measures that.

commits.message:
[levanter] Count attention-map FLOPs with and without causal masking (#11122)

Count forward attention-map FLOPs per token using every key in each
layer's full or sliding-window span, as Levanter's existing MFU does, or
only the keys retained by causal masking: `min(i + 1, span)` for query
`i`. Both totals are averaged over the sequence and summed across
layers.

#11123 uses these counts in Snowball and June synthetic benchmark
reporting.

Part of #9812

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[rl] Support colocated expert-block weight sync (#11104)

Enable expert-block weight synchronization when a Megatron policy and a
local vLLM engine share one four-H100 node. The launcher accepts the
standard training entrypoint with policy TP=PP=ETP=1 EP=4, one vLLM
TP=PP=1 DP=EP=4 engine, NCCL weight-sync configuration, TRITON MoE, and
transfer verification. Other colocated layouts and entrypoints fail
before GPU allocation.

The receiver's physical GPU placement is checked against the trainer at
every update. Level-2 sleep releases inference weights during training;
after the weight wake, transfer groups are rebuilt, verified, and closed
before generation resumes. Colocated groups use Gloo CUDA broadcasts
because the pinned NCCL 2.29 rejects two ranks on one GPU. Separate-GPU
transfers retain NCCL. Marin's preflight mirrors the runtime's four-GPU
limit because the SkyRL runtime is packaged separately.

The affected Marin tests (84) and the SkyRL launch-config tests (49)
pass. The [four-H100
gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/42649704508/job/129272421482)
reported one passing colocated test in 5m40s. It ran two
train/sleep/wake/sync/generation updates and compared each rank's dense
and expert weights exactly with a fresh vLLM checkpoint load, plus a
fixed-input prompt log-probability within 2e-3. The separate-GPU
expert-block case passed in the earlier full Grug run before the
colocated NCCL failure was fixed.

Fixes #10380

[skyrl] Remove dedicated SGLang support (#11230)

Rationale: It's better to rm sglang code (& potentially dig out from git
if needed) than to have agent maintain / evolve code that we don't use /
test.
___
🤖Remove dedicated SGLang engine construction, sampling translation,
weight loading and validation from the vendored runtime. Keep vLLM's
local and remote paths, generic OpenAI-compatible clients, parameter
pass-through, and nested and flat error responses.

Extract and adapt the SGLang changes from #10660; its critic, FlashQLA
and other cleanup remain separate. The recipe special-token and
stop-token fix in #11229 applies cleanly, and its nine regressions pass
with this removal.

The SkyRL CPU suite passed 433 tests in its frozen environment,
including six HTTP regressions, and 15 recipe/topology combinations
produced identical configs to main. A [one-H100
smoke](https://iris-cw-us-east-02a.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fromain%2Fsglang-h100-publication-a2-01a1cd47)
started vLLM with compilation and CUDA graphs enabled, generated, then
published 311 tensors including a modified `model.norm.weight`. All
1,024 values in that norm matched the published values exactly. The next
eight tokens carried the updated policy version. Iris downgraded the
requested interactive priority to batch. The GPU smoke uses one local
serving rank and CUDA IPC weight transfer; remote generation and
weight-update requests have CPU HTTP coverage.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[catalog] Require measured snapshot counts for Daytona-safety verdicts (#11200)

Follow-up to #11197 implementing the measured-count requirement for the
Daytona-safety field: no agentic safe/unsafe verdict is accepted without
a
measured count.

Measurement runs the production naming path instead of reimplementing
it.
shellbox gains `snapshot_identity(source, resources)` — it validates the
source
the way `_prepare` does (rejecting `ADD` Dockerfiles and Dockerfiles
outside the
context root) and derives the deterministic name, and `_snapshot` now
calls it.
Harbor gains `machine_spec()`, the pure task-config to `MachineSpec`
mapping that
`start()` now uses. The Atlas counter materializes each pinned task's
environment, loads the task's own `task.toml` through Harbor's
`EnvironmentConfig`,
builds the spec through Harbor's mapping, and counts distinct production
names.
Tasks the production validation rejects are reported as failures and are
not
counted safe. The parallel identity implementation and its fidelity test
are
deleted; behavior tests now sit at the shared functions, and the
identity test
runs in the isolated harbor lane beside the acquisition tests.

The projection rejects inferred verdicts: an agentic safe/unsafe without
`daytona_snapshot_count` and `daytona_count_basis` collapses to
`unassessed`,
and every recorded count carries the `DAYTONA_SAFE_SNAPSHOT_LIMIT`
threshold.
Publication propagates the count, basis and threshold together with the
verdict
onto carried-forward sources.

Measuring through the production path corrected four records:

- CalibForge V1 is 2,205 distinct snapshots, not 2,181. Every task names
its own
prebuilt registry image in `task.toml`, so production uses the registry
reference and never the `environment/` build context the earlier FROM
census
  counted.
- SWE-Gym is unsafe at 2,163, not safe at one. All 2,438 rows share one
Dockerfile, but 2,163 carry distinct per-task `setup_repo.sh` payloads
that
  the earlier `dockerfile_id` grouping could not see.
- MiMo music is unsafe at 1,000, not safe at one: its tasks share a base
image
  but not a build context.
- `laion/toolscale-v4` is 4,048, not 32 — the earlier probe stopped once
the
  count passed ten and reported the partial value.

Counts re-measured over pinned payloads: OpenSWE 36,884 and 8,436;
R2E-Gym
8,101; MiMo code 2,698, cyber 1,000, general 989, music 1,000 (all
unsafe);
MiMo webdev one; SWE-Gym 2,163; forty INPUT slices at one; nine more
slices
between two and seven; `toolscale` 4,048. SWE-Smith admitted stays safe
at five
contexts, and CalibForge shared-v2 stays at two public verifier
contexts, with
the 23 provisioning variants cited from the campaign capacity record
because the
public payloads carry no per-task resource shapes.

Two records stay deliberately short of a production count. `Harbor
Hub:skill2env`
now reads `unassessed`: its old count came from an eleven-task sample of
a
7,496-task cohort, which is not a cohort measurement. The two converted
repositories keep their counts with the basis naming the conversion
ledger's
per-task build-context inventory, which the conversion program's own
production-named recount will confirm.

The vendored Harbor edit is a fork-local change to the Daytona
environment
adapter; per the forking policy it lands in the same pull request as its
caller.

Known gap, not addressed here: the repository has no code path for
deleting
Daytona snapshots. Cleanup is manual, per `.agents/ops/daytona.md`.
Measurement
never creates a snapshot, but any run that does create them still needs
an
operator to reclaim them; building that path is separate work.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[skyrl] Preserve Harbor trajectories after context rejection (#11235)

Keep the sampled Harbor conversation when a later prompt exceeds the
context limit. Previously, the rejected new conversation became the last
rollout record, so training lost the earlier sampled tokens and Harbor's
verifier grade. Treat the rejection as recoverable after a sampled turn
so the rollout engine leaves the earlier sampled record intact. A
rejected first request still ends with a length stop.

Trials that finish without an agent exception retain their tokens,
logprobs, loss mask, and verifier reward in training. Recorded agent
exceptions can still zero the training reward under Harbor's configured
error policy. Mini-SWE still needs its separate fix to stop retrying
rejected requests.

Adapted from
[5dc90b5](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/5dc90b5df0b3c499240c6e488968d4747fc0f591)
in #11199. The worker regression fails on main and passes with the fix.
The dedicated SkyRL CPU lane passes all 432 tests.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[skyrl] Load Grug routed experts from checkpoint keys (#11130)

Load Grug routed experts according to the checkpoint's tensor keys. One
67B checkpoint declares artifact schema 2 for its shared-expert layout
but stores stacked routed-expert tensors. Megatron-Bridge selected
numbered routed-expert names from the schema flag and skipped the absent
weights, yielding logits that disagreed with vLLM.

The bridge now keeps the config's shared-expert architecture and selects
the routed mapping from the weight index. On eight frozen responses
(1,141 scored tokens; [input
rows](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-rno2a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fopd-interference%2Fphase1b%2F2026.11.09.6%2Fdiagnostics%2Ftrain200%2FR_train_8_short.jsonl)),
Megatron chosen-token NLL is 0.1537 nats/token versus vLLM's 0.1543
([vLLM
result](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-rno2a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fopd-interference%2Fphase1b%2F2026.11.09.6%2Fdiagnostics%2Ftrain200%2Fvllm_m1_parity.json),
[Megatron
result](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-rno2a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fopd-interference%2Fphase1b%2F2026.11.09.7%2Fdiagnostics%2Fm1-loader-parity%2Fscores%2FM1%2Fscore-0000.json));
the old load gave 3.2273. Corrected KL(T1‖M1) on 1,000 terminal turns
fell from 2.237 to 0.0955 nats/token ([score
shards](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-rno2a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fopd-interference%2Fphase1b%2F2026.11.09.7%2Fscores%2FM1-P_J%2F)),
reversing the previous disjointness result.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[skyrl] Honor recipe special-token and stop-token settings (#11229)

Honor configured `skip_special_tokens` in vLLM requests, and let
training and evaluation recipes set it alongside multiple
`stop_token_ids`. Omitted settings retain special-token stripping and
existing stopping behavior. Supplied stop IDs already passed through
translation.

The old behavior had two causes:

- [Upstream SkyRL #192](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/192)
enabled stripping so markers such as `<|im_end|>` would not reach
environments through `env.step()`. The hardcoded `True` also overrode an
explicit `False`. The [original
review](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/pull/192#discussion_r2296877686)
suggested the configuration lookup with a `True` fallback used here.
- Both recipe fields were absent from the defaults. Structured
composition rejects undeclared keys; [MarinSkyRL
#734](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/734) introduced
the current merger. An earlier [Delphi pilot,
#67](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/67), hit the
same missing-key error in Hydra. It removed the recipe setting because
training kept the token IDs and its boxed-answer grader did not need
special-token text.

One CPU regression covers recipe composition and vLLM request
translation for training and evaluation. Both cases fail on main and
with the old hardcoded flag, and pass with the fix. A [12-case
Qwen3-0.6B
smoke](https://iris-cw-us-east-02a.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fromain%2Fskyrl-sampling-smoke-a2-01a1ccb4)
on one H100 with existing pins verified returned text, token IDs and
stop reasons for both sampling sections, with compilation and CUDA
graphs enabled. It exercised the real vLLM engine API. Iris
automatically downgraded the requested interactive priority to batch.
The vLLM translation and sampling defaults are unchanged from the
smoke-tested revision.

Supersedes #11225.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[rl] Mirror Hub models on CPU while retaining node fallback (#11161)

Mirror the Hugging Face policy, local-inference teachers, and Hub draft
model on the Iris CPU coordinator before submitting the GPU job. Record
pinned mirror locations in the resolved config; nodes restore policy and
teacher snapshots from those locations, and drafts read the bucket
mirror directly. Mirrors use the node download’s file types and only
indexed shards when a safetensors index is present. Unsupported
non-safetensors layouts log a warning and retain node-side Hub fallback
for policies and teachers.

Keep the existing cache TTL and lock-free warm return. Missing markers
or missing files listed in the mirror manifest retain node-side Hub
fallback, including repair of partially expired draft mirrors. This
moves normal model downloads off allocated GPUs without changing retry
behavior when a mirror expires. A policy or teacher mirror with expired
shards and a surviving marker can still pass the coordinator’s lock-free
warm check; nodes then download from the Hub on later launches until
that marker also expires. This retains main’s download cost for partial
expiry; the stacked TTL follow-up repairs it under the lock. Recorded
mirrors carry the CPU-resolved commit for node fallback, with requested
aliases restored for offline loading. Unmirrored unsupported layouts
retain main’s requested-revision fallback. Snapshot installation uses a
node-local lock and adds files atomically without removing existing
tokenizer or template files. Existing weights are reused; truncated
shards are replaced.

The CPU launcher requires Iris job context for Hub inputs; run the
experiment entry point with `--run`. PREPARE remains download-free. A
separate policy tokenizer permits a model-only mirror, while local
teachers still require their embedded tokenizer.

TTL refresh and removing the Hub fallback are in the stacked follow-up
#11118.

Part of #9233.
